page.text:
The Fundamental Theorem of Linear Maps—the Rank-Nullity
Theorem—establishes the conservation of dimension under linear mappings:
the dimension of the domain is apportioned precisely between the
directions compressed to zero (the nullity) and the directions preserved
in the target space (the rank).
